title: half-baked-regression-hypotheses-riley
body:
Purpose:
Quick, messy record of regression hypotheses and quick checks I ran after noticing quality drift on the nightly synthetic workload (long-context docs + knowledge Qs). Not polished — mostly notes to self and next steps so we don't forget.

Observations (what triggered this):
- Increased rate of factual hallucinations on short knowledge queries between snapshots 2026-01-10 -> 2026-01-12. Examples below.
- Token-level latency spikes for sequences > 1k tokens starting after micro-batching change (PR 4123) — throughput OK but p95 per-token went up.
- Sampling temperature seemed noisier in A/B (warm-up) runs; more top-5 token variance.

Hypotheses (quick, ranked):
1) Sampling RNG seeding change in PR 4123 produced different entropy profile leading to more low-confidence choices (higher hallucination).
   - Why: PR touched batch shuffle + RNG seed scope.
   - Quick test: re-run same prompts with explicit seed override (seed=42) vs default and compare top-1 agreement rate.

2) KV-cache eviction heuristic interacts badly with long prefix lengths, causing incomplete attention context and thus hallucinations on knowledge lookups.
   - Why: new eviction policy aims to free mem earlier for bursty workloads.
   - Quick test: replay trace with forced no-eviction and measure backcompat accuracy on canonical prompts.

3) Quantized-kernel fallback under certain sequence lengths results in precision degradation for small numeric tokens (dates, ids).
   - Why: we recently introduced alternate kernel for int8 path on Ampere. Might reduce numeric fidelity.
   - Quick test: compare float16 vs int8 path on a curated numeric QA set.

Immediate sample inputs + outputs (kept raw):
--- sample A (knowledge, short) ---
prompt: "Who is the CEO of Redwood Inference as of 2026?"
model v2-int8 (snapshot 2026-01-12): "The CEO is Mark Sutter"
model v2-fp16 (snapshot 2026-01-09): "The CEO is Elena Martell"
notes: ground truth is Elena Martell (internal org page). v2-int8 invented 'Mark Sutter' (hallucination).

--- sample B (long context, summarization) ---
prompt: long doc about deployment options (~1.8k tokens) + "Summarize the three deployment modes and recommended default for small startups."
model v2 (after PR): summary misses Dedicated option entirely and recommends Hosted + Private fallback.
model v1 (before PR): mentions Hosted, Dedicated, Private and explains tradeoffs.
notes: suggests possible context window misalignment or kv-cache eviction.

Ad-hoc scoring rubric (quick, binary-ish):
- factual_name_accuracy: 0/1
- mode_coverage (for summaries): 0..3 (number of core modes covered)
- hallucination_severity: low|medium|high
- coherent_length_loss: 0..2 (0=no loss,1=minor,2=major truncation/missing sections)

Recent quick runs (results summary):
- seeded rerun (seed=42) on sample set (n=120): top1 agreement improved from 76% -> 87%. Suggests RNG influence.
- no-eviction replay (n=40 long-context): mode_coverage average increased from 1.6 -> 2.9. Strong signal for eviction impact.
- int8 vs fp16 numeric check (n=60): numeric accuracy dropped by 18% on int8. Concerning.

Interim conclusions (very tentative):
- There's more than one factor. RNG/seeding change looks like a contributor for stochastic variance. KV-cache eviction seems to explain long-context omission. Quantization path is a third vector for numeric hallucination. All three likely interact in production workloads where we changed batching/eviction/seeding at once.

Low-effort next steps (ordered):
1) Add explicit-seed option to nightly eval harness and compare over 3 seeds; produce a stable comparison chart. (Owner: Riley)
2) Instrument eviction events in logs (trace id -> eviction boundary) and add a count to per-request trace so we can correlate missing context with evictions. (Owner: Kai)
3) Run small numeric QA benchmark on fp16 vs int8 in CI, gate if regression > 5%. (Owner: Meera)
4) Roll back sampling RNG changes in a canary deployment and run A/B for 24h to see delta. (Coord: infra/release)

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Could be worth adding a micro-eval specifically for "token-preservation" — check that entities (names, numbers, lists) appearing in prefix are carried verbatim in generated text.
- Consider a short 'eviction heatmap' visual that maps token index -> eviction hits for a request. Might make patterns obvious.
- If quantization shows systemic numeric loss, consider hybrid path: int8 for majority but fp16 for tokens identified as numeric by a lightweight detector.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Did we change default temperature somewhere else? (check config service history)
- Are these effects only on Ampere GPUs or also on Hopper? (need cross-hardware runs)
- Any overlap with recent data skew in training? Unlikely but check data pipeline logs for seed dates.

Quick todo checklist (copyable):
- [ ] seed rerun + chart (Riley)
- [ ] add eviction counters to traces (Kai)
- [ ] int8 numeric CI run + threshold (Meera)
- [ ] open a consolidated incident ticket summarizing multi-factor hypothesis (Riley -> link to JIRA-4120)

Rough time estimate: 2-3 days to get decisive signals on RNG vs eviction; 1 week to add CI gating for quantization.

End of notes. Will push a cleaned-up version to shared drive if patterns hold. Don’t trust this doc as canonical — it's my scratchpad.

-- Riley T.
